errors.text: The hypothesis substitutes refractory HfNbTaTiZr or CoCrFeMnNi systems for the relevant sub-10 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, despite their very different structures, cohesive energies, and surface-segregation tendencies.
It assigns structural evolution to SRO percolation and precipitation rather than the observed surface-energy-driven Au/Cu segregation, active diffusion, melting, and evaporation.
The claim that nanoparticle surfaces lower the activation barrier for SRO formation and produce percolating clusters is an unsupported extrapolation from bulk or periodic-cell simulations.
Evidence E1 is misinterpreted: the Cr-Hf precipitate exists at low temperature and vanishes near 620 K; it does not demonstrate precipitation being triggered at 620 K.

The proposed measurements do not directly determine elemental self-diffusivity, surface enrichment, or volatile-element loss, so they cannot cleanly test the relevant assumption of sluggish versus active diffusion.
